reader.requirement: The scope of an IF ends at the END-IF at its own nesting level, at a separator period, or, when nested, at an ELSE belonging to an enclosing IF, with ELSE and END-IF each matched to the nearest preceding unmatched, unterminated IF (GR3 as amended), and statement-1/statement-2 may be imperative or conditional statements whose own scope the ELSE also ends; the witnesses cover END-IF matching, nested ELSE/END-IF and phrase association.

edition-consulted.switches: ConstructRegistry.IsAvailable(edition, format) decides which statement a [NOT] conditional phrase inside statement-1 belongs to; it does not touch ELSE, END-IF or the period
NEXT SENTENCE archaic warning COBOL0903 at 2023 only; silent at 1985

reader.edition-search: ifStatement carries no semantic predicate; grep Edition|DialectLevel in ConditionalPhrases.cs (Associates/MayAssociate only), CobolErrorStrategy.cs (keyword printing and reserved words, not IF scope) and ControlFlowBinder.BindIf (none).
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: IF scope termination is the same greedy parse at every edition
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the four witnesses cover END-IF and ELSE matching and phrase association; a three-level IF ended by one ELSE, ELSE ending a conditional ADD inside statement-1, and NEXT SENTENCE inside a nested IF ended by ELSE are probed here

probes.printed: W1 W2 Y3 Z3B Q4 W5 V5 X6 W6 SE7 N 9 Y8 W9 T10; EXPECT: MATCH (if1.out)
probes.expected: a: END-IF ends the IF and the next statement runs; b: one period ends two nested IFs; c: an outer ELSE ends inner IFs of one and two levels; an ELSE ends ADD ... ON SIZE ERROR inside statement-1; NEXT SENTENCE in a nested IF goes past the period

probes.printed: COBOL2269 second ELSE; COBOL0306 END-IF after a period, and a second END-IF, without a matching IF; COBOL2072 ELSE with no statement-1
probes.expected: refused: an END-IF or ELSE with no unterminated IF to match

probes.expected: §1985:VI.6.16.3 SR3 forbids NEXT SENTENCE with END-IF: a lead for that syntax rule, not for GR1

reader.notes: Scope termination is the parse: statementBlock is statement+ and ANTLR binds ELSE and END-IF greedily to the innermost open IF, which is the amended GR3 matching; a period ends every open IF through sentence. LEAD outside this rule: §1985:VI.6.16.3 SR3 (no NEXT SENTENCE with END-IF) is not enforced at --std 85 (ifr3.cob, exit 0); the grammar comment at CobolControlFlow.g4 lines 202-206 records accepting it as a 2023 determination under kb/Work PB396, which does not weigh 1985's explicit SR3.

refuter.evidence: refute-1985-107/rif-001 at --std 85, EXPECT: MATCH (rif.out): END-IF ends a conditional ADD ... ON SIZE ERROR in statement-2 and the IF (S1 AFTER1); ELSE ends a SEARCH ... AT END ... WHEN inside statement-1 (F2, and E2B on the false branch); an inner END-IF followed by the outer ELSE and END-IF (Y3, Z3B); inner IF/ELSE/END-IF then outer END-IF and a following statement (Y4 Z4 W4); ELSE matched to the outer IF after NOT ON SIZE ERROR holding a delimited IF (N5 AFTER5 6); three nested IFs, END-IF closing only the innermost, two ELSEs matched to the next unmatched IFs, period ending the rest (Y6 AFTER6). Each is the amended GR3 matching and GR1a/b/c. No later-edition IF phrase exists for 1985 to refuse; the 1985-only reading is the NEXT SENTENCE surrogate, covered by the reader's if1. cite.py: OK §1985:VI.6.16.4 GR1c the text is in GR1c; OK §1985:VI.6.16.4 GR3 the text is in GR3. The reader's lead stands outside this rule: §1985:VI.6.16.3 SR3 (no NEXT SENTENCE with END-IF) is not enforced at --std 85 (ifr3.cob), an under-rejection of SR3, not of GR1's scope termination.
